intent: Hold the open state of one menu of actions and tie the trigger that opens it to the popup that lists them.
typical_uses: A "more actions" button on a row, a card or a toolbar
An account menu behind an avatar or a user name

dont_use_when.situation: Picking one value for a form field from a fixed list
A menu opened by right-clicking or long-pressing an area rather than by a trigger button
A persistent horizontal row of application menus, such as File, Edit and View
A long list of commands the user filters by typing
A floating panel with fields or other controls to operate
Site or application navigation between pages

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
While open, pressing Escape or pressing outside the popup closes the menu and reports the change through `onOpenChange`.

While a modal menu (`modal`, true when not given) is open, page scroll is locked and pointer interaction with elements outside the menu is disabled; with `modal={false}` the rest of the page stays usable, except while the menu was opened by hovering a trigger with `openOnHover`, which neither locks scroll nor blocks the page.

anti_patterns.dont: Hold the open state in the caller and pass `open` without `onOpenChange`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `onOpenChange` alongside `open` and update the state from it, or leave both out; a controlled `open` that nothing updates keeps the menu from opening on a trigger press or closing on Escape

children.states: children is the root's content, either React nodes or a function of the active trigger's payload that returns them
children.because: `React.ReactNode | PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` - the function form receives `{ payload }` from whichever trigger opened the menu. A React node and a function have no JSON Schema representation.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (such as a trigger press, an item press, an outside press or Escape). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with imperative `close` and `unmount` actions
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<MenuRoot.Actions | null>` - a ref object holding functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Menu.createHandle(), shared with a trigger placed outside this root
handle.because: `MenuHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the menu's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

triggerId.states: triggerId is the id of the trigger a controlled menu is open for, or null
triggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

defaultTriggerId.states: defaultTriggerId is the id of the trigger an initially open menu is open for, or null
defaultTriggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

good.title: A menu of row actions behind an outline button
A menu opened from state the caller owns

bad.title: A reading direction passed to the root, as an older menu library took it
bad.why: The root takes no `dir`; the menu's arrow-key navigation reads the reading direction from the nearest DirectionProvider, so wrap the right-to-left subtree in one instead.
